description: Reproducibility metadata for the APS weight-sensitivity analysis (manuscript Sec. 6 / Table 11), captured at execution time. Modeled on the ReproducibilityMetadata schema used throughout the Voynich statistical-auditing framework (dsh_framework).
pandas_version: 3.0.2 (installed but not used by this script)
git_commit_note: Not captured: analysis was run outside a git-tracked working copy. Recommended action before archiving: commit aps_sensitivity_load_data.py and aps_sensitivity_analysis.py to the new APS OSF repository and re-run this capture so git_commit is populated.
framework_version: n/a (standalone sensitivity script, not part of dsh_framework versioning)
doi: TBD -- new APS-specific OSF repository not yet created
input_dataset_provenance: 13 anchors from the pre-existing Voynich OSF calibration repository (calibration/<anchor>/results/*.json, unmodified) plus the Voynich manuscript's own s1-s5 values taken directly from Table 9 of the manuscript (not recomputed).
analysis_scripts: aps_sensitivity_load_data.py  (loads/aggregates s1-s5 per anchor, cross-checks against Table 10 APS)
aps_sensitivity_analysis.py   (OAT and global weight-perturbation sensitivity analysis, N=5000 draws)
perturbation_method: Global: each baseline weight multiplied by a factor drawn uniform(0.6, 1.4), then renormalized to sum to 1 (N=5000 draws). OAT: each weight varied +-30% in 13 steps, remaining four weights renormalized proportionally.
known_limitation: Sensitivity analysis uses per-anchor MEAN s1-s5 across replicates, not full replicate-level resampling; it isolates weight uncertainty from data uncertainty by design (see manuscript Sec. 6.2).
